text: Tamers, I adore your work. I watch every single episode you make multiple times, I come home religiously to watch your videos on the Fridays you post them, elated that my day now sucks less because a new Tamers video exists. I have roped my friends into this pattern as well, they are all Tamerspilled because of how much I won't stop praising your videos. Outside of the act of posting your art publicly, perhaps you are not asking for criticism, and I am sure you don't need my permission to completely disregard what I say. But if you're interested, I feel like I gotta say something (and it's out of admiration when I say it). The stallion episodes recently feel extremely different from the mare episodes, and I am certain that's on purpose. But my criticism; it's nothing about the subject matter, it is the writing itself, namely the dialogue. Scenes that appear as though they are meant to be sincere, dramatic even, are so much longer, often now fully elaborating through character dialogue every emotion and idea being conveyed. It feels like I am being spoon fed every aspect of the relationship turmoil and resolution they face. It's to the detriment of the balance of the episode. I love the whiplash of humor into a serious moment. You have already shown your writing prowess, early on, that you can tell me things about a character's underlying difficulties in a 10 second moment. The episode right before this comes to mind: Starlight Glimmer says, "I don't think that way because I don't know the first thing about love." It's not a very drawn out scene, but suddenly I feel like she becomes a deeper character. She goes from 'the character manipulating another one ruthlessly' to 'the manipulator that does it because she doesn't know any other way to hold onto her relationships (her relationships that she doesn't seem to even fully know why she feels the need to cling to them, she's that confused)'. Compare this to Apple Split or Care Package fully articulating multiple times their thoughts and mistakes in a situation and their every emotion in response to them. I feel less like I am learning about a funny character providing a glimpse of insight and vulnerability and more like you are directly explaining to me, the viewer, what the character is. Couldn't I have gleaned, for example, from prior experiences with Apple Split that he is being sincere during their wedding despite forcing Care Package to wear a dress in so fewer words? When it comes to dialogue, less is often more. If it's all meticulously laid out like that, in the nicest way possible, I'm almost waiting for the scene to end so the episode can move on from the thing I already understand. I think you're probably aware that it runs long at times given how several times when the monologue ends you disrupt it with a joke to lighten the mood. I think you wouldn't have to lighten the mood if the drama was already sparingly applied. I don't want to make it sound like I know what you think though. This is your work, I respect it immensely, I support you regardless, but that's the one thing I really want to say that leans towards the negative. I seriously hope this comes across as somebody familiar with your work and not just somebody showing up to sling opinions your way without knowing where they are. I love uber gay Sombra though, he was my favorite thing in the episode, that parts not really relevant, I just wanted to say that too.

author: @marcusthepastownerofspidereeze

replies.text:
I never properly explained it in a video I think, but my headcanon is that when Soarin is in his crazy alicorn state, he's actually mirroring the image of the Big Mac he sees in his head, which he used to see as the most evil abuser ever. Because when he first met Big Mac he saw him abusing Braeburn. so right after when he got his alicorn powers, to save braeburn from Big Mac, Soarin lets his own possessiveness side come out and take control and the craziness comes about because he's also being influenced by his Alicorn magic which is twisted because he's overcome with emotions. Basically when he wears his Big Mac cloak he's like (Big Mac was an evil abuser who got everything he wanted to abusing braeburn, if I can do that to protect braeburn then I''ll be just as evil and twisted as big mac). Even though Soarin, Big mac, and braeburn have all made up that side of him still comes out sometimes, especially when he's in a fight.

If you look at Braeburn's personality it's the opposite to Soarin. Where when he's using his alicorn powers where he's super emotional normally, but I draw his eyes locked in try not to have him show much emotion to try and symbolize how with his alicorn powers he's not going to let anyone abuse him again
